comparisons.peer_summary: UTB balances affecting the effective tax rate were $573 million at December 31, 2024, with a possible decrease of up to $217 million in the next 12 months. The Corporation recognized an interest benefit of $9 million in 2024 and had accruals for interest and penalties of $105 million at year-end 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose the potential variability in their unrecognized tax benefits (UTB) balances over the next 12 months due to audit settlements. However, JPMorgan quantifies a symmetric range (increase or decrease) of approximately $2.4 billion, whereas Bank of America quantifies only a potential decrease of up to $217 million, indicating a significantly smaller range of potential variability in Bank of America's disclosures compared to JPMorgan.

sentences.text: The evaluation of unrecognized tax benefits as well as the potential for audit settlements make it reasonably possible that over the next 12 months the gross balance of unrecognized tax benefits may increase or decrease by as much as approximately $2.4 billion.
The change in the unrecognized tax benefit would result in a payment or income statement recognition.

At December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, the balance of the Corporation's UTBs which would, if recognized, affect the Corporation's effective tax rate was $573 million, $671 million and $709 million, respectively.

It is reasonably possible that the UTB balance may decrease by as much as $217 million during the next 12 months, since resolved items will be removed from the balance whether their resolution results in payment or recognition.
